Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA - explicit 'no training' language + subprocessors / transfers

Ben —

Thanks for the demo last week. Legal and procurement asked us to get the DPA finalized before we move to the trial environment. Two specific asks from Clearwell: 1) an explicit prohibition on Redwood using any customer-provided data (including prompts, attachments, or derived outputs) to train or improve models; 2) a current subprocessor registry and a commitment that any new subprocessor that could access customer data will require prior written consent or a 30-day notice and approval right.

I attached our initial redlines (Clearwell_DPA_redlines_v1.pdf) — we called for an absolute ban on training / model tuning and no transfers to jurisdictions outside the US/EU without consent. We also need to understand the technical flows (where logs are stored, telemetry used for observability, and how KV cache is handled). Can you confirm scope and provide a suggested counter-redline?

Best,
Laura

Subject: Re: DPA - explicit 'no training' language + subprocessors / transfers

Laura —

Thanks — appreciate the clarity. High level: Redwood is comfortable agreeing to a contractual prohibition on using Customer Data to *train* or *fine-tune* models, with narrowly scoped operational exceptions for (a) debugging/incident investigation, (b) anonymized telemetry for service health, and (c) aggregated, de-identified metrics that cannot be tied back to a customer. We propose language that prohibits model improvement (weights updates, fine-tuning, retraining) on Customer Data, while allowing non-training telemetry and anonymized analytics.

On subprocessors, we can provide the current registry and commit to 30-day notice for changes; we generally avoid asking for consent on every hire but will commit to consent for any subprocessor that would have the ability to access PII or Content. For transfers, Redwood relies on SCCs for EU transfers where relevant and can discuss restrictions for transfers outside EU/US.

Looping in legal and security to propose concrete redlines (cc'd). I can also set a short call if that helps.

Next steps: Marissa/Neha — please see Clearwell redlines attached and propose counter language that maps to the 'no training' ask while preserving necessary operational exceptions. Vivek — I'll coordinate onboarding timing once legal signs off.

Thanks,
Ben

Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: Draft redlines for Clearwell 'no-train' clause

Team —

I reviewed Clearwell's redlines. High level comments: we can accept a contractual ban on training where 'training' is defined as any process that updates model weights or creates customer-specific fine-tuned models. We should explicitly permit: (1) ephemeral caching/KV usage required to serve requests (no weight updates), (2) aggregated/anonymous telemetry for reliability and billing, and (3) transformation/formatting of responses (e.g., sanitization, prompt templating) so product continues to function.

Proposed language (short form):
"Customer Data shall not be used to train or improve the weights or architecture of any machine learning model, nor to produce customer-targeted fine-tuned models. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood may use aggregated, de-identified telemetry and operational logs solely to maintain, debug, monitor, and optimize the service, provided such data cannot be re-associated with Customer or individual end users."

Require: KMS controls for customer-supplied keys (if requested), SOC2 evidence, and that any subprocessor with logical access to Content requires either prior consent or a 30-day notice and opt-out for material changes. For international transfers, we propose SCCs + transfer impact assessment; reject a blanket ban on transfers to all non-US/EU regions but will accept contractual notice and review.

Attached: Redwood_proposed_DPA_redline_v2.docx (contains exact redline markup).

Ben —

Thanks for the quick turn. We've reviewed internal counsel feedback and have a few sticking points: Clearwell needs an absolute prohibition on any use of Customer Content to improve models (no exceptions). While we appreciate the operational arguments, procurement cannot accept telemetry exceptions that could be used to recreate prompts or customer context. We are willing to permit aggregated billing metrics, but require an explicit carve-out barring any telemetry that includes prompt/response content or identifiers.

Additionally, Clearwell requires that any subprocessor with the ability to access Content is pre-approved; notice alone is insufficient for us. We also require a commitment that transfers to non-approved jurisdictions will not occur without Clearwell's prior written consent. Please find our counter (Clearwell_redlines_v2.pdf) attached; major edits are highlighted in red.

Is Redwood prepared to sign an execution-ready DPA if we accept the 'no-train' wording in a stricter form (and Redwood accepts pre-approval for Content-accessing subprocessors)?

Regards,
Laura

Subject: Executed DPA & next steps for trial environment (DocuSign complete)

Laura —

Thanks for working through the redlines. We reached a mutually acceptable compromise: Redwood has agreed to an explicit contractual prohibition on using Customer Content to train or fine-tune our models, and to limit telemetry to aggregated, de-identified metrics that cannot be re-associated with Clearwell or its end users. Per agreement, any subprocessor that could access Content requires prior written approval (we provided the current registry and will provide 30 days' notice for changes; for subprocessors with Content access we will request approval and will not onboard without consent). For transfers, Redwood will rely on SCCs for EU transfers and will not transfer to non-approved jurisdictions without prior written consent.

DocuSign has been completed by both parties — attached is the executed DPA (Executed_DPA_Clearwell_20270607.pdf) and the final subprocessor registry (Subprocessor_Registry_20270607.csv). Link to DocuSign envelope: https://app.docusign.com/CLW-2027-0423

Next steps: Vivek — please coordinate trial provisioning for Clearwell (test tenant, API keys, onboarding checklist). Legal has asked that we maintain a 30-day change-notice log for subprocessors and provide SOC 2 and encryption attestations during onboarding.
